tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

1	# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)
2	
3	Accessors (global -> VM):
4	  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
5	  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
6	  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
7	  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
8	  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
9	  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
10	  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
11	Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
12	`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).
13	
14	Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
15	  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
16	  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
17	                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
18	  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
19	  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
20	  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
21	Import paths:
22	  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
23	  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
24	  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
25	  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())
26	
27	Traits:
28	  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
29	  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
30	  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
31	  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
32	  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.
33	
34	Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
35	  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
36	      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }
37	
38	Decisions taken while fixing the shared core (apply everywhere):
39	  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
40	      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.
41	  AddressUtils::verify_call_result_from_target(context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>, target, result)
42	  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())
43	  Erc1967Utils: every fn that reads/writes a slot or emits/gets msg value takes `context` first:
44	      get_implementation(context), get_admin(context), change_admin(context, new_admin),
45	      get_beacon(context), upgrade_to_and_call(context, impl, data), upgrade_beacon_to_and_call(context, beacon, data)
46	  IEip712: `pub trait IEip712: HostAccess` (no #[public], it has associated consts);
47	      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.
48	  Interface wrappers from sol_interface!: f(context.vm(), Call::new()/Call::new_mutating(self)/..., args).
49	      Static calls use Call::new() (no storage borrow needed).
50	Test fixtures: contracts/src/test_utils.rs exports ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE (const Address).

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

schema.name: Agent
schema.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

1	# Module migration brief (read fully before editing)
2	
3	Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust). We are migrating from Stylus SDK 0.9.0 +
4	motsu test framework to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 + the SDK's own testing framework (`stylus-test`,
5	exposed as `stylus_sdk::testing::*`, i.e. `TestVM`), on Rust 1.91.0 stable.
6	
7	Your worktree is the path given in your task. It is based on git commit 7e36233, which
8	already moved the manifests and the shared core (utils/address, utils/storage_slot,
9	proxy/erc1967/utils, utils/cryptography/eip712) to the new API. The crate does not
10	compile yet: other agents own the other modules and are fixing them in parallel.
11	
12	Read first:
13	- /tmp/bench/notes/api-map.md : the API decisions. Follow them exactly.
14	- The SDK source (read-only reference, do NOT build or run anything inside it):
15	  /tmp/bench/downloads/stylus-sdk-rs-0.10.10 . Useful paths: stylus-core/src/host.rs (VM
16	  accessor traits), stylus-core/src/calls/ (call contexts), stylus-sdk/src/call/ (call
17	  functions), stylus-test/README.md (TestVM usage), examples/ (SDK example contracts).
18	
19	## Ownership
20	Edit ONLY the files in your ownership list (given in your task). If you need a change in
21	a file you do not own, do not make it: list it under "requests" in your final report.
22	Never change a public item's name. Signature changes are allowed only as in api-map.md
23	or when needed to remove a global accessor (then document it in your report).
24	
25	## What "done" means for your files
26	1. Non-test code compiles on SDK 0.10.10 with NO global accessors: no `msg::`, `evm::`,
27	   `block::`, `contract::` free functions, no `stylus_sdk::call::{Error, MethodError, Call,
28	   StaticCallContext}` (use `stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::{Error, MethodError}`;
29	   `Call`/`StaticCallContext` come from `stylus_sdk::prelude::*`). Host access is
30	   `self.vm()` (HostAccess) or the `context` parameter.
31	2. Every `pub trait I...` that is a public interface is tagged `#[public]`, and every
32	   `impl Trait for X` of such a trait is tagged `#[public]`. Traits with associated consts
33	   are NOT `#[public]`. Routed methods must be written in the `#[public] impl` block itself:
34	   default bodies in a `#[public]` trait are not routed.
35	3. Every motsu test is converted to a plain `#[test]` using `stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM`:
36	     let vm = TestVM::default();
37	     let mut c = Token::from(&vm);
38	     vm.set_sender(ALICE);            // msg::sender
39	     vm.set_value(U256::from(1));     // msg::value
40	     vm.set_block_timestamp(..); vm.set_chain_id(..); vm.set_balance(addr, v);
41	     vm.get_emitted_logs(); vm.mock_call(..); vm.mock_delegate_call(..); vm.mock_static_call(..)
42	   Use `crate::test_utils::{ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE}` instead of motsu's injected accounts.
43	   motsu's `Contract::<T>::new()` + `.sender(alice)` become `T::from(&vm)` + `vm.set_sender`.
44	   Property tests (proptest inside a test) must build a fresh TestVM per case.
45	4. Preserve every test scenario and every assertion. Do NOT delete, weaken, or merge away a
46	   test unless it is an exact duplicate of another test in the same file (then say so).
47	   Keep `#[should_panic]`/revert checks as revert checks (`is_err()` / matching the error).
48	5. Do NOT change storage layout: field order and field types of every `#[storage]`
49	   struct stay byte-for-byte the same. (Proxies depend on it.)
50	6. Preserve the public ABI: function names, selectors, parameter and return types, error
51	   types and their encodings. Preserve behavior. Only the Rust-level API for host access
52	   may change (documented in the report).
53	7. Rustdoc stays accurate: where the call pattern changed (context/self.vm()), update the
54	   doc text. No commented-out code, no TODO left for things you were asked to do.
55	8. `#[cfg(test)]` modules use `use super::*;` and explicit imports as the rest of the repo.
56	
57	## Verification (use the 1.91.0 toolchain; never use nightly for building)
58	- Check your files only:
59	    cd <worktree> && cargo +1.91.0 check -p openzeppelin-stylus > /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log 2>&1
60	    grep -A1 '^error' /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log | grep -- '--> ' | sed 's/.*--> //' | sort | uniq -c
61	  Only errors in YOUR files matter until the whole crate compiles.
62	- Tests: `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib <filter>` runs only once the whole
63	  test target compiles. Until then, check your test code with
64	  `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib --no-run` and filter errors to your files.
65	- Formatting: `rustfmt +nightly-2025-08-01 --edition 2021 <your files>` (the repo's
66	  rustfmt.toml uses options only nightly rustfmt supports). Run it on your files at the end.
67	- Clippy (once the crate compiles): `cargo +1.91.0 clippy -p openzeppelin-stylus --all-targets -- -D warnings`
68	  Lints are pedantic (see workspace Cargo.toml). Fix warnings in your files.
69	
70	## Git
71	- Work and commit on your branch (already created for your worktree). Small logical commits,
72	  message style: `refactor(<area>): <what>` or `test(<area>): <what>`. Each message ends with:
73	    Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
74	- Commit only your files. Do not push. Do not switch branches. Do not run `git reset --hard`
75	  or any command that touches other worktrees.
76	
77	## Final report (your last message, at most 40 lines)
78	- Files changed; commit list (`git log --oneline 7e36233..HEAD`).
79	- Signature changes (name: old -> new).
80	- Test inventory: number of test functions before (`git show 7e36233:<file> | grep -cE '#\[(motsu::)?test\]'`)
81	  and after, per file; any test you merged or removed (with reason).
82	- Compile status of your files (lib / tests); whether the crate compiled as a whole at the time.
83	- Requests to other owners; blockers; anything you were unsure about.
84

1	# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)
2	
3	Accessors (global -> VM):
4	  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
5	  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
6	  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
7	  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
8	  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
9	  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
10	  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
11	Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
12	`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).
13	
14	Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
15	  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
16	  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
17	                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
18	  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
19	  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
20	  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
21	Import paths:
22	  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
23	  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error

28	  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
29	  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
30	  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
31	  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
32	  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.

1	//! Module with an interface required for smart contract in order to receive
2	//! ERC-721 token transfers.
3	#![allow(missing_docs)]
4	#![cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]
5	use alloc::{vec, vec::Vec};
6	
7	use alloy_primitives::{aliases::B32, Address, U256};
8	use openzeppelin_stylus_proc::interface_id;
9	use stylus_sdk::{abi::Bytes, function_selector, prelude::*};
10	
11	/// The expected value returned from [`IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`].
12	pub const RECEIVER_FN_SELECTOR: B32 = B32::new(function_selector!(
13	    "onERC721Received",
14	    Address,
15	    Address,
16	    U256,
17	    Bytes,
18	));
19	
20	sol_interface! {
21	    /// [`super::Erc721`] token receiver Solidity interface.
22	    ///
23	    /// Check [`super::IErc721Receiver`] trait for more details.
24	    interface IErc721ReceiverInterface {
25	        /// See [`super::IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`].
26	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
27	        function onERC721Received(
28	            address operator,
29	            address from,
30	            uint256 token_id,
31	            bytes calldata data
32	        ) external returns (bytes4);
33	    }
34	}
35	
36	/// [`super::IErc721`] token receiver trait.
37	///
38	/// Interface for any contract that wants to support
39	/// [`super::IErc721::safe_transfer_from`]
40	/// and [`super::IErc721::safe_transfer_from_with_data`] from ERC-721 asset
41	/// contracts.
42	#[interface_id]
43	#[public]
44	pub trait IErc721Receiver {
45	    /// This function is called whenever an [`super::Erc721`] `token_id`
46	    /// token is transferred to this contract via
47	    /// [`super::IErc721::safe_transfer_from`] or
48	    /// [`super::IErc721::safe_transfer_from_with_data`].
49	    ///
50	    /// It must return its its Solidity selector to confirm the token transfer.
51	    /// If any other value is returned or the interface is not implemented
52	    /// by the recipient, the transfer will be reverted.
53	    ///
54	    /// # Arguments
55	    ///
56	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
57	    /// * `operator` - Account of the operator.
58	    /// * `from` - Account of the sender.
59	    /// * `token_id` - Token id as a number.
60	    /// * `data` - Additional data with no specified format.
61	    ///
62	    /// # Errors
63	    ///
64	    /// * May return a custom error.
65	    fn on_erc721_received(
66	        &mut self,
67	        operator: Address,
68	        from: Address,
69	        token_id: U256,
70	        data: Bytes,
71	    ) -> Result<B32, Vec<u8>>;
72	}

10	/// An [`Erc721`] token that can be burned (destroyed).

14	    /// The error type associated to this trait implementation.
15	    type Error: Into<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>;
16	
17	    /// Burns `token_id`.
18	    /// The approval is cleared when the token is burned.
19	    ///
20	    /// # Arguments
21	    ///
22	    /// * `value` - Amount to be burnt.
23	    ///
24	    /// # Errors
25	    ///
26	    /// * [`erc721::Error::NonexistentToken`] - If token does not exist.
27	    /// * [`erc721::Error::InsufficientApproval`] - If the caller does not have
28	    ///   the right to approve.
29	    ///
30	    /// # Events
31	    ///
32	    /// * [`erc721::Transfer`].
33	    fn burn(&mut self, token_id: U256) -> Result<(), Self::Error>;
34	}
35	
36	#[public]
37	impl IErc721Burnable for Erc721 {
38	    type Error = erc721::Error;
39	
40	    fn burn(&mut self, token_id: U256) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
41	        // Setting an "auth" arguments enables the
42	        // [`super::super::Erc721::_is_authorized`] check which verifies that
43	        // the token exists (from != [`Address::ZERO`]).
44	        //
45	        // Therefore, it is not needed to verify that the return value is not 0
46	        // here.
47	        self._update(Address::ZERO, token_id, self.vm().msg_sender())?;
48	        Ok(())
49	    }
50	}

1	//! Optional `Enumerable` extension of the ERC-721 standard.
2	//!
3	//! This implements an optional extension of [`super::super::Erc721`] defined in
4	//! the EIP that adds enumerability of all the token ids in the contract as well
5	//! as all token ids owned by each account.
6	//!
7	//! CAUTION: [`super::super::Erc721`] extensions that implement custom
8	//! [`super::super::Erc721::balance_of`] logic, such as `Erc721Consecutive`,
9	//! interfere with enumerability and should not be used together with
10	//! [`Erc721Enumerable`].
11	
12	use alloc::{vec, vec::Vec};
13	
14	use alloy_primitives::{aliases::B32, uint, Address, U256};
15	use openzeppelin_stylus_proc::interface_id;
16	pub use sol::*;
17	use stylus_sdk::{stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError, prelude::*, storage::{StorageMap, StorageU256, StorageVec}};
18	
19	use crate::{
20	    token::erc721::{self, IErc721},
21	    utils::introspection::erc165::IErc165};
22	
23	#[cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]
24	mod sol {
25	    use alloy_sol_macro::sol;
26	
27	    sol! {
28	        /// Indicates an error when an `owner`'s token query
29	        /// was out of bounds for `index`.
30	        ///
31	        /// NOTE: The owner being [`Address::ZERO`]
32	        /// indicates a global out of bounds index.
33	        #[derive(Debug)]
34	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
35	        error ERC721OutOfBoundsIndex(address owner, uint256 index);
36	
37	        /// Indicates an error related to batch minting not allowed.
38	        #[derive(Debug)]
39	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
40	        error ERC721EnumerableForbiddenBatchMint();
41	    }
42	}
43	
44	/// An [`Erc721Enumerable`] extension error.
45	#[derive(SolidityError, Debug)]
46	pub enum Error {
47	    /// Indicates an error when an `owner`'s token query
48	    /// was out of bounds for `index`.
49	    ///
50	    /// NOTE: The owner being [`Address::ZERO`]
51	    /// indicates a global out of bounds index.
52	    OutOfBoundsIndex(ERC721OutOfBoundsIndex),
53	
54	    /// Indicates an error related to batch minting not allowed.
55	    EnumerableForbiddenBatchMint(ERC721EnumerableForbiddenBatchMint)}
56	
57	impl MethodError for Error {
58	    fn encode(self) -> alloc::vec::Vec<u8> {
59	        self.into()
60	    }
61	}
62	
63	/// State of an [`Erc721Enumerable`] contract.
64	#[storage]
65	pub struct Erc721Enumerable {
66	    /// Maps owners to a mapping of indices to tokens ids.
67	    pub(crate) owned_tokens: StorageMap<Address, StorageMap<U256, StorageU256>>,
68	    /// Maps tokens ids to indices in `owned_tokens`.
69	    pub(crate) owned_tokens_index: StorageMap<U256, StorageU256>,
70	    /// Stores all tokens ids.
71	    pub(crate) all_tokens: StorageVec<StorageU256>,
72	    /// Maps indices at `all_tokens` to tokens ids.
73	    pub(crate) all_tokens_index: StorageMap<U256, StorageU256>}

75	/// This is the interface of the optional `Enumerable` extension
76	/// of the ERC-721 standard.
77	#[interface_id]
78	#[public]
79	pub trait IErc721Enumerable {
80	    /// The error type associated to this ERC-721 enumerable trait
81	    /// implementation.
82	    type Error: Into<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>;
83	
84	    /// Returns a token ID owned by `owner` at a given `index` of its token
85	    /// list.
86	    ///
87	    /// Use along with [`super::super::Erc721::balance_of`] to enumerate all of
88	    /// `owner`'s tokens.
89	    ///
90	    /// # Arguments
91	    ///
92	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
93	    /// * `owner` - Address of token's owner.
94	    /// * `index` - Index of the token at `owner`'s tokens list.
95	    ///
96	    /// # Errors
97	    ///
98	    /// * [`Error::OutOfBoundsIndex`] - If an `owner`'s token query is out of
99	    ///   bounds for `index`.
100	    fn token_of_owner_by_index(
101	        &self,
102	        owner: Address,
103	        index: U256,
104	    ) -> Result<U256, Self::Error>;
105	
106	    /// Returns the total amount of tokens stored by the contract.
107	    ///
108	    /// # Arguments
109	    ///
110	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
111	    fn total_supply(&self) -> U256;
112	
113	    /// Returns a token ID at a given `index` of all the tokens
114	    /// stored by the contract.
115	    ///
116	    /// Use along with [`Self::total_supply`] to
117	    /// enumerate all tokens.
118	    ///
119	    /// # Arguments
120	    ///
121	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
122	    /// * `index` - Index of the token in all tokens list.
123	    ///
124	    /// # Errors
125	    ///
126	    /// * [`Error::OutOfBoundsIndex`] - If an `owner`'s token query is out of
127	    ///   bounds for `index`.
128	    fn token_by_index(&self, index: U256) -> Result<U256, Self::Error>;
129	}

135	#[public]
136	impl IErc721Enumerable for Erc721Enumerable {
137	    type Error = Error;
138	
139	    fn token_of_owner_by_index(
140	        &self,
141	        owner: Address,
142	        index: U256,
143	    ) -> Result<U256, Self::Error> {
144	        let token = self.owned_tokens.getter(owner).get(index);
145	
146	        if token.is_zero() {
147	            Err(ERC721OutOfBoundsIndex { owner, index }.into())
148	        } else {
149	            Ok(token)
150	        }
151	    }
152	
153	    fn total_supply(&self) -> U256 {
154	        let tokens_length = self.all_tokens.len();
155	        U256::from(tokens_length)
156	    }
157	
158	    fn token_by_index(&self, index: U256) -> Result<U256, Self::Error> {
159	        self.all_tokens.get(index).ok_or(
160	            ERC721OutOfBoundsIndex { owner: Address::ZERO, index }.into(),
161	        )
162	    }
163	}

173	impl Erc721Enumerable {
174	    /// Function to add a token to this extension's
175	    /// ownership-tracking data structures.
176	    ///
177	    /// # Arguments
178	    ///
179	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
180	    /// * `to` - Address representing the new owner of the given `token_id`.
181	    /// * `token_id` - ID of the token to be added to the tokens list of the
182	    ///   given address.
183	    /// * `erc721` - Read access to a contract providing [`IErc721`] interface.
184	    ///
185	    /// # Errors
186	    ///
187	    /// * [`erc721::Error::InvalidOwner`] - If owner address is
188	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`].
189	    pub fn _add_token_to_owner_enumeration(
190	        &mut self,
191	        to: Address,
192	        token_id: U256,
193	        erc721: &impl IErc721<Error = erc721::Error>,
194	    ) -> Result<(), erc721::Error> {
195	        let length = erc721.balance_of(to)? - uint!(1_U256);
196	        self.owned_tokens.setter(to).setter(length).set(token_id);
197	        self.owned_tokens_index.setter(token_id).set(length);
198	
199	        Ok(())
200	    }
201	
202	    /// Function to add a token to this extension's token
203	    /// tracking data structures.
204	    ///
205	    /// # Arguments
206	    ///
207	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
208	    /// * `token_id` - ID of the token to be added to the tokens list.
209	    pub fn _add_token_to_all_tokens_enumeration(&mut self, token_id: U256) {
210	        let index = self.total_supply();
211	
212	        self.all_tokens_index.setter(token_id).set(index);
213	        self.all_tokens.push(token_id);
214	    }
215	
216	    /// Function to remove a token from this extension's
217	    /// ownership-tracking data structures.
218	    ///
219	    /// Note that while the token is not assigned a new owner,
220	    /// the `self.owned_tokens_index` mapping is NOT updated:
221	    /// this allows for  gas optimizations e.g.
222	    /// when performing a transfer operation (avoiding double writes).
223	    ///
224	    /// This has O(1) time complexity, but alters the order
225	    /// of the `self.owned_tokens` array.
226	    ///
227	    /// # Arguments
228	    ///
229	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
230	    /// * `from` - Address representing the previous owner of the given
231	    ///   `token_id`.
232	    /// * `token_id` - ID of the token to be removed from the tokens list of the
233	    ///   given address.
234	    /// * `erc721` - Read access to a contract providing [`IErc721`] interface.
235	    ///
236	    /// # Errors
237	    ///
238	    /// * [`erc721::Error::InvalidOwner`] - If owner address is
239	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`].
240	    pub fn _remove_token_from_owner_enumeration(
241	        &mut self,
242	        from: Address,
243	        token_id: U256,
244	        erc721: &impl IErc721<Error = erc721::Error>,
245	    ) -> Result<(), erc721::Error> {
246	        // To prevent a gap in from's tokens array,
247	        // we store the last token in the index of the token to delete,
248	        // and then delete the last slot (swap and pop).
249	        let last_token_index = erc721.balance_of(from)?;
250	        let token_index = self.owned_tokens_index.get(token_id);
251	
252	        let mut owned_tokens_by_owner = self.owned_tokens.setter(from);
253	
254	        // When the token to delete is the last token,
255	        // the swap operation is unnecessary.
256	        if token_index != last_token_index {
257	            let last_token_id = owned_tokens_by_owner.get(last_token_index);
258	
259	            // Move the last token to the slot of the to-delete token.
260	            owned_tokens_by_owner.setter(token_index).set(last_token_id);
261	            // Update the moved token's index.
262	            self.owned_tokens_index.setter(last_token_id).set(token_index);
263	        }
264	
265	        // This also deletes the contents at the last position of the array.
266	        self.owned_tokens_index.delete(token_id);
267	        owned_tokens_by_owner.delete(last_token_index);
268	
269	        Ok(())
270	    }
271	
272	    /// Function to remove a token from this extension's
273	    /// token tracking data structures.
274	    ///
275	    /// This has O(1) time complexity,
276	    /// but alters the order of the `self.all_tokens` array.
277	    ///
278	    /// # Arguments
279	    ///
280	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
281	    /// * `token_id` -  ID of the token to be removed from the tokens list.
282	    ///
283	    /// # Panics
284	    ///
285	    /// * The function should not panic in a regular way.
286	    pub fn _remove_token_from_all_tokens_enumeration(
287	        &mut self,
288	        token_id: U256,
289	    ) {
290	        // To prevent a gap in the tokens array,
291	        // we store the last token in the index of the token to delete,
292	        // and then delete the last slot (swap and pop).
293	        let last_token_index = U256::from(self.all_tokens.len() - 1);
294	        let token_index = self.all_tokens_index.get(token_id);
295	
296	        // When the token to delete is the last token,
297	        // the swap operation is unnecessary.
298	        // However, since this occurs so
299	        // rarely (when the last minted token is burnt)
300	        // that we still do the swap here
301	        // to avoid the gas cost of adding an 'if' statement
302	        // (like in `self._remove_token_from_owner_enumeration`).
303	        let last_token_id = self
304	            .all_tokens
305	            .get(last_token_index)
306	            .expect("token at given index must exist");
307	
308	        // Move the last token to the slot of the to-delete token.
309	        self.all_tokens
310	            .setter(token_index)
311	            .expect("slot at given `token_index` must exist")
312	            .set(last_token_id);
313	
314	        // Update the moved token's index.
315	        self.all_tokens_index.setter(last_token_id).set(token_index);
316	
317	        // This also deletes the contents at the last position of the array.
318	        self.all_tokens_index.delete(token_id);
319	        self.all_tokens.pop();
320	    }

322	    /// See [`erc721::Erc721::_increase_balance`].
323	    /// Check if tokens can be minted in batch.
324	    ///
325	    /// Mechanism to be consistent with [Solidity version](https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts/blob/v5.0.0/contracts/token/ERC721/extensions/ERC721Enumerable.sol#L163-L171)
326	    ///
327	    /// # Arguments
328	    ///
329	    /// * `amount` - The number of tokens to increase balance.
330	    ///
331	    /// # Errors
332	    ///
333	    /// * [`Error::EnumerableForbiddenBatchMint`] - If an `amount` is greater
334	    ///   than `0`.
335	    pub fn _check_increase_balance(amount: u128) -> Result<(), Error> {
336	        if amount > 0 {
337	            Err(ERC721EnumerableForbiddenBatchMint {}.into())
338	        } else {
339	            Ok(())
340	        }
341	    }
342	}

43	/// An [`Erc721Wrapper`] error.
44	#[derive(SolidityError, Debug)]
45	pub enum Error {
46	    /// Indicates that an address can't be an owner.
47	    /// For example, [`Address::ZERO`] is a forbidden owner in [`Erc721`].
48	    /// Used in balance queries.
49	    InvalidOwner(erc721::ERC721InvalidOwner),
50	    /// Indicates a `token_id` whose `owner` is the zero address.
51	    NonexistentToken(erc721::ERC721NonexistentToken),
52	    /// Indicates an error related to the ownership over a particular token.
53	    /// Used in transfers.
54	    IncorrectOwner(erc721::ERC721IncorrectOwner),
55	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `sender`. Used in transfers.
56	    InvalidSender(erc721::ERC721InvalidSender),
57	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `receiver`. Used in transfers.
58	    InvalidReceiver(erc721::ERC721InvalidReceiver),
59	    /// Indicates a failure with the token `receiver`, with the reason
60	    /// specified by it.
61	    InvalidReceiverWithReason(erc721::InvalidReceiverWithReason),
62	    /// Indicates a failure with the `operator`’s approval. Used in transfers.
63	    InsufficientApproval(erc721::ERC721InsufficientApproval),
64	    /// Indicates a failure with the `approver` of a token to be approved. Used
65	    /// in approvals.
66	    InvalidApprover(erc721::ERC721InvalidApprover),
67	    /// Indicates a failure with the `operator` to be approved. Used in
68	    /// approvals.
69	    InvalidOperator(erc721::ERC721InvalidOperator),
70	    /// The received ERC-721 token couldn't be wrapped.
71	    UnsupportedToken(ERC721UnsupportedToken),
72	    /// An operation with an ERC-721 token failed.
73	    Erc721FailedOperation(Erc721FailedOperation)}
74	
75	impl From<erc721::Error> for Error {
76	    fn from(value: erc721::Error) -> Self {
77	        match value {
78	            erc721::Error::InvalidOwner(e) => Error::InvalidOwner(e),
79	            erc721::Error::NonexistentToken(e) => Error::NonexistentToken(e),
80	            erc721::Error::IncorrectOwner(e) => Error::IncorrectOwner(e),
81	            erc721::Error::InvalidSender(e) => Error::InvalidSender(e),
82	            erc721::Error::InvalidReceiver(e) => Error::InvalidReceiver(e),
83	            erc721::Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason(e) => {
84	                Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason(e)
85	            }
86	            erc721::Error::InsufficientApproval(e) => {
87	                Error::InsufficientApproval(e)
88	            }
89	            erc721::Error::InvalidApprover(e) => Error::InvalidApprover(e),
90	            erc721::Error::InvalidOperator(e) => Error::InvalidOperator(e)}
91	    }
92	}

111	/// Interface of an extension of the ERC-721 token contract that supports token
112	/// wrapping.
113	#[interface_id]
114	#[public]
115	pub trait IErc721Wrapper: IErc721Receiver {
116	    /// The error type associated to this trait implementation.
117	    type Error: Into<alloc::vec::Vec<u8>>;
118	
119	    /// Allow a user to deposit underlying tokens and mint the corresponding
120	    /// `token_ids`.
121	    ///
122	    /// # Arguments
123	    ///
124	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
125	    /// * `account` - The account to deposit tokens to.
126	    /// * `token_ids` - List of underlying token ids to deposit.
127	    ///
128	    /// # Errors
129	    ///
130	    /// * [`Error::Erc721FailedOperation`] - If the underlying token is not an
131	    ///   ERC-721 contract.
132	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason`] - If an error occurs during
133	    ///   [`erc721::IErc721::transfer_from`] operation on the underlying token.
134	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSender`] - If `token_id` already exists.
135	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If `to` is [`Address::ZERO`].
136	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If
137	    ///   [`erc721::IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] hasn't returned its
138	    ///   interface id or returned with an error.
139	    fn deposit_for(
140	        &mut self,
141	        account: Address,
142	        token_ids: Vec<U256>,
143	    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error>;
144	
145	    /// Allow a user to burn wrapped tokens and withdraw the corresponding
146	    /// `token_ids` of the underlying tokens.
147	    ///
148	    /// # Arguments
149	    ///
150	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
151	    /// * `account` - The account to withdraw tokens to.
152	    /// * `token_ids` - List of underlying token ids to withdraw.
153	    ///
154	    /// # Errors
155	    ///
156	    /// * [`Error::Erc721FailedOperation`] - If the underlying token is not an
157	    ///   ERC-721 contract.
158	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason`] - If an error occurs during
159	    ///   [`erc721::IErc721::safe_transfer_from`] operation on the underlying
160	    ///   token.
161	    /// * [`Error::NonexistentToken`] - If the token does not exist and `auth`
162	    ///   is not [`Address::ZERO`].
163	    /// * [`Error::InsufficientApproval`] - If `auth` is not [`Address::ZERO`]
164	    ///   and `auth` does not have a right to approve this token.
165	    fn withdraw_to(
166	        &mut self,
167	        account: Address,
168	        token_ids: Vec<U256>,
169	    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error>;
170	
171	    /// Returns the underlying token.
172	    ///
173	    /// # Arguments
174	    ///
175	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
176	    #[must_use]
177	    fn underlying(&self) -> Address;
178	}

180	impl Erc721Wrapper {
181	    /// Constructor.
182	    ///
183	    /// # Arguments
184	    ///
185	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
186	    /// * `underlying_token` - The wrapped token.
187	    pub fn constructor(&mut self, underlying_token: Address) {
188	        self.underlying.set(underlying_token);
189	    }
190	
191	    /// Check [`IErc721Wrapper::deposit_for()`] for more information.
192	    #[allow(clippy::missing_errors_doc)]
193	    pub fn deposit_for(
194	        &mut self,
195	        account: Address,
196	        token_ids: Vec<U256>,
197	        erc721: &mut Erc721,
198	    ) -> Result<bool, Error> {
199	        let sender = self.vm().msg_sender();
200	        let contract_address = self.vm().contract_address();
201	        let underlying = Erc721Interface::new(self.underlying());
202	
203	        for token_id in token_ids {
204	            // This is an "unsafe" transfer that doesn't call any hook on
205	            // the receiver. With [`IErc721Wrapper::underlying()`] being trusted
206	            // (by design of this contract) and no other contracts expected to
207	            // be called from there, we are safe.
208	            match underlying.transfer_from(
209	                Call::new_in(self),
210	                sender,
211	                contract_address,
212	                token_id,
213	            ) {
214	                Ok(()) => (),
215	                Err(e) => {
216	                    if let stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error::Revert(ref reason) = e {
217	                        if !reason.is_empty() {
218	                            return Err(Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason(
219	                                erc721::InvalidReceiverWithReason {
220	                                    reason: String::from_utf8_lossy(reason)
221	                                        .to_string()},
222	                            ));
223	                        }
224	                    }
225	                    return Err(Error::Erc721FailedOperation(
226	                        Erc721FailedOperation { token: self.underlying() },
227	                    ));
228	                }
229	            }
230	
231	            erc721._safe_mint(account, token_id, &vec![].into())?;
232	        }
233	
234	        Ok(true)
235	    }
236	
237	    /// Check [`IErc721Wrapper::withdraw_to()`] for more information.
238	    #[allow(clippy::missing_errors_doc)]
239	    pub fn withdraw_to(
240	        &mut self,
241	        account: Address,
242	        token_ids: Vec<U256>,
243	        erc721: &mut Erc721,
244	    ) -> Result<bool, Error> {
245	        let sender = self.vm().msg_sender();
246	        let underlying = Erc721Interface::new(self.underlying());
247	
248	        for token_id in token_ids {
249	            // Setting the `auth` argument enables the `_is_authorized` check
250	            // which verifies that the token exists (from != 0).
251	            // Therefore, it is not needed to verify that the return value is
252	            // not 0 here.
253	            erc721._update(Address::ZERO, token_id, sender)?;
254	            match underlying.safe_transfer_from(
255	                Call::new_in(self),
256	                self.vm().contract_address(),
257	                account,
258	                token_id,
259	                vec![].into(),
260	            ) {
261	                Ok(()) => (),
262	                Err(e) => {
263	                    if let stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error::Revert(ref reason) = e {
264	                        if !reason.is_empty() {
265	                            return Err(Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason(
266	                                erc721::InvalidReceiverWithReason {
267	                                    reason: String::from_utf8_lossy(reason)
268	                                        .to_string()},
269	                            ));
270	                        }
271	                    }
272	                    return Err(Error::Erc721FailedOperation(
273	                        Erc721FailedOperation { token: self.underlying() },
274	                    ));
275	                }
276	            }
277	        }
278	
279	        Ok(true)
280	    }
281	
282	    /// Allow minting on direct ERC-721 transfers to this contract.
283	    ///
284	    /// # Arguments
285	    ///
286	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
287	    /// * `operator` - The operator of the transfer.
288	    /// * `from` - The sender of the transfer.
289	    /// * `token_id` - The token id of the transfer.
290	    /// * `data` - The data of the transfer.
291	    /// * `erc721` - Write access to an [`Erc721`] contract.
292	    ///
293	    /// # Errors
294	    ///
295	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedToken`] - If `self.vm().msg_sender()` is not the underlying
296	    ///   token.
297	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSender`] - If `token_id` already exists.
298	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If `to` is [`Address::ZERO`].
299	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If
300	    ///   [`erc721::IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] hasn't returned its
301	    ///   interface id or returned with an error.
302	    pub fn on_erc721_received(
303	        &mut self,
304	        _operator: Address,
305	        from: Address,
306	        token_id: U256,
307	        _data: &Bytes,
308	        erc721: &mut Erc721,
309	    ) -> Result<B32, Error> {
310	        let sender = self.vm().msg_sender();
311	        if self.underlying() != sender {
312	            return Err(Error::UnsupportedToken(ERC721UnsupportedToken {
313	                token: sender}));
314	        }
315	
316	        erc721._safe_mint(from, token_id, &vec![].into())?;
317	
318	        Ok(RECEIVER_FN_SELECTOR)
319	    }
320	
321	    /// Check [`IErc721Wrapper::underlying()`] for more information.
322	    #[must_use]
323	    pub fn underlying(&self) -> Address {
324	        self.underlying.get()
325	    }
326	
327	    /// Mints wrapped tokens to cover any underlying tokens that would have been
328	    /// function that can be exposed with access control if desired.
329	    ///
330	    /// # Arguments
331	    ///
332	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
333	    /// * `account` - The account to mint tokens to.
334	    /// * `token_id` - A mutable reference to the Erc20 contract.
335	    /// * `erc721` - Write access to an [`Erc721`] contract.
336	    ///
337	    /// # Errors
338	    ///
339	    /// * [`Error::Erc721FailedOperation`] - If the underlying token is not a
340	    ///   [`Erc721`] contract, or the contract fails to execute the call.
341	    /// * [`Error::IncorrectOwner`] - If the underlying token is not owned by
342	    ///   the contract.
343	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSender`] - If `token_id` already exists.
344	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If `to` is [`Address::ZERO`].
345	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If
346	    ///   [`erc721::IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] hasn't returned its
347	    ///   interface id or returned with an error.
348	    fn _recover(
349	        &mut self,
350	        account: Address,
351	        token_id: U256,
352	        erc721: &mut Erc721,
353	    ) -> Result<U256, Error> {
354	        let underlying = Erc721Interface::new(self.underlying());
355	
356	        let owner = underlying.owner_of(Call::new_in(self), token_id).map_err(
357	            |_| {
358	                Error::Erc721FailedOperation(Erc721FailedOperation {
359	                    token: self.underlying()})
360	            },
361	        )?;
362	
363	        let contract_address = self.vm().contract_address();
364	        if owner != contract_address {
365	            return Err(erc721::Error::IncorrectOwner(
366	                erc721::ERC721IncorrectOwner {
367	                    sender: contract_address,
368	                    token_id,
369	                    owner},
370	            )
371	            .into());
372	        }
373	
374	        erc721._safe_mint(account, token_id, &vec![].into())?;
375	
376	        Ok(token_id)
377	    }
378	}

432	        &mut self,
433	        from: Address,
434	        to: Address,
435	        token_id: U256,
436	        data: Bytes,
437	    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
438	        self.transfer_from(from, to, token_id)?;
439	        self._check_on_erc721_received(self.vm().msg_sender(), from, to, token_id, &data)
440	    }

444	        from: Address,

446	        token_id: U256,
447	    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
448	        if to.is_zero() {
449	            return Err(
450	                ERC721InvalidReceiver { receiver: Address::ZERO }.into()
451	            );

454	        // Setting an "auth" argument enables the `_is_authorized` check which
455	        // verifies that the token exists (`from != 0`). Therefore, it is
456	        // not needed to verify that the return value is not 0 here.
457	        let previous_owner = self._update(to, token_id, self.vm().msg_sender())?;
458	        if previous_owner != from {
459	            return Err(ERC721IncorrectOwner {
460	                sender: from,
461	                token_id,
462	                owner: previous_owner}
463	            .into());
464	        }
465	        Ok(())
466	    }

469	        &mut self,
470	        to: Address,
471	        token_id: U256,
472	    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
473	        self._approve(to, token_id, self.vm().msg_sender(), true)
474	    }

477	        &mut self,
478	        operator: Address,
479	        approved: bool,
480	    ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
481	        self._set_approval_for_all(self.vm().msg_sender(), operator, approved)
482	    }

485	        self._require_owned(token_id)?;
486	        Ok(self._get_approved(token_id))

490	        self.operator_approvals.get(owner).get(operator)

content.content:
"examples/eddsa",
]
exclude = ["fuzz", "templates/crypto-erc20"]

# Explicitly set the resolver to version 2, which is the default for packages
# with edition >= 2021.
# https://doc.rust-lang.org/edition-guide/rust-2021/default-cargo-resolver.html
resolver = "2"

[workspace.package]
authors = ["OpenZeppelin"]
edition = "2021"
license = "MIT"
repository = "https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/rust-contracts-stylus"
version = "0.3.0"

[workspace.lints.rust]
missing_docs = "warn"
unreachable_pub = "warn"
rust_2021_compatibility = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
unexpected_cfgs = { level = "warn", check-cfg = ['cfg(coverage_nightly)'] }

[workspace.lints.clippy]
pedantic = "warn"
all = "warn"

[workspace.dependencies]
# Stylus SDK related
stylus-sdk = "=0.10.10"
# Devnet tooling used by the end-to-end tests and benches (dev-only).
stylus-tools = { version = "=0.10.10", features = ["integration-tests"] }

# `alloy` is used by the end-to-end tests and benches. The contracts only depend
# on `alloy-primitives` and `alloy-sol-types`, which must match the versions the
# Stylus SDK is built against.
alloy = { version = "=1.7.3", features = ["essentials", "signer-local"] }
alloy-primitives = { version = "=1.5.7", default-features = false, features = [
  "tiny-keccak",
] }
alloy-sol-types = { version = "=1.5.7", default-features = false }
alloy-sol-macro = { version = "=1.5.7", default-features = false }

ruint = "^1.17.1"

eyre = "0.6.8"
keccak-const = "0.2.0"
rand = "0.9.0"
regex = "1.10.4"
tiny-keccak = { version = "2.0.2", features = ["keccak"] }
tokio = { version = "1.45", features = ["full"] }
futures = "0.3.30"
num-traits = "0.2.14"
zeroize = { version = "1.8.1", features = ["derive"] }
proptest = "1"
educe = "0.6.0"
hex-literal = "0.4.1"
sha2 = "0.10.9"
static_assertions = "1.1.0"

# procedural macros
syn = { version = "2.0.58", features = ["full"] }
proc-macro2 = "1.0.79"
quote = "1.0.35"

# members
e2e = { path = "lib/e2e" }
e2e-proc = { path = "lib/e2e-proc" }
openzeppelin-stylus = { path = "contracts" }
openzeppelin-stylus-proc = { path = "contracts-proc", version = "=0.3.0" }
openzeppelin-crypto = { path = "lib/crypto" }

[profile.release]
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"
opt-level = "z"
strip = true

exclude = ["fuzz", "templates/crypto-erc20"]

# Explicitly set the resolver to version 2, which is the default for packages
# with edition >= 2021.
# https://doc.rust-lang.org/edition-guide/rust-2021/default-cargo-resolver.html
resolver = "2"

[workspace.package]
authors = ["OpenZeppelin"]
edition = "2021"
license = "MIT"
repository = "https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/rust-contracts-stylus"
version = "0.3.0"

[workspace.lints.rust]
missing_docs = "warn"
unreachable_pub = "warn"
rust_2021_compatibility = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
unexpected_cfgs = { level = "warn", check-cfg = ['cfg(coverage_nightly)'] }

[workspace.lints.clippy]
pedantic = "warn"
all = "warn"

[workspace.dependencies]
# Stylus SDK related
stylus-sdk = "=0.10.10"
# Devnet tooling used by the end-to-end tests and benches (dev-only).
stylus-tools = { version = "=0.10.10", features = ["integration-tests"] }

# `alloy` is used by the end-to-end tests and benches. The contracts only depend
# on `alloy-primitives` and `alloy-sol-types`, which must match the versions the
# Stylus SDK is built against.
alloy = { version = "=1.7.3", features = ["essentials", "signer-local"] }
alloy-primitives = { version = "=1.5.7", default-features = false, features = [
  "tiny-keccak",
] }
alloy-sol-types = { version = "=1.5.7", default-features = false }
alloy-sol-macro = { version = "=1.5.7", default-features = false }

ruint = "^1.17.1"

eyre = "0.6.8"
keccak-const = "0.2.0"
rand = "0.9.0"
regex = "1.10.4"
tiny-keccak = { version = "2.0.2", features = ["keccak"] }
tokio = { version = "1.45", features = ["full"] }
futures = "0.3.30"
num-traits = "0.2.14"
zeroize = { version = "1.8.1", features = ["derive"] }
proptest = "1"
educe = "0.6.0"
hex-literal = "0.4.1"
sha2 = "0.10.9"
static_assertions = "1.1.0"

# procedural macros
syn = { version = "2.0.58", features = ["full"] }
proc-macro2 = "1.0.79"
quote = "1.0.35"

# members
e2e = { path = "lib/e2e" }
e2e-proc = { path = "lib/e2e-proc" }
openzeppelin-stylus = { path = "contracts" }
openzeppelin-stylus-proc = { path = "contracts-proc", version = "=0.3.0" }
openzeppelin-crypto = { path = "lib/crypto" }

[profile.release]
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"
opt-level = "z"
strip = true
lto = true
debug = false
rpath = false
debug-assertions = false
incremental = false

[profile.dev]
panic = "abort"

[workspace.metadata.typos]
default = { extend-ignore-identifiers-re = [
  # ignore hex data samples.
  "[0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]",
] }
files = { extend-exclude = [] }

1	//! Implementation of the ERC-2309 "Consecutive Transfer Extension" as defined
2	//! in [ERC-2309].
3	//!
4	//! This extension allows the minting large batches of tokens, during
5	//! contract construction only. For upgradeable contracts, this implies that
6	//! batch minting is only available during proxy deployment, and not in
7	//! subsequent upgrades. These batches are limited to 5000 tokens at a time by
8	//! default to accommodate off-chain indexers.
9	//!
10	//! Using this extension removes the ability to mint single tokens during
11	//! contract construction. This ability is regained after construction. During
12	//! construction, only batch minting is allowed.
13	//!
14	//! Fields `first_consecutive_id` (used to offset first token id) and
15	//! `max_batch_size` (used to restrict maximum batch size) can be assigned
16	//! during construction.
17	//!
18	//! [ERC-2309]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2309

307	    /// Override of [`Erc721::_owner_of`] that checks the sequential
308	    /// ownership structure for tokens that have been minted as part of a
309	    /// batch, and not yet transferred.
310	    ///
311	    /// # Arguments
312	    ///
313	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
314	    /// * `token_id` - Token id as a number.
315	    pub fn _owner_of(&self, token_id: U256) -> Address {
316	        let owner = self.erc721._owner_of(token_id);
317	        // If token is owned by the core, or beyond consecutive range, return
318	        // base value.
319	        if !owner.is_zero()
320	            || token_id < U256::from(self._first_consecutive_id())
321	            || token_id > U256::from(U96::MAX)
322	        {
323	            return owner;
324	        }
325	
326	        // Otherwise, check the token was not burned, and fetch ownership from
327	        // the anchors.
328	        if self.sequential_burn.get(token_id) {
329	            Address::ZERO
330	        } else {
331	            // NOTE: Bounds already checked. No need for safe cast of token_id
332	            self.sequential_ownership.lower_lookup(U96::from(token_id)).into()
333	        }
334	    }

336	    /// Mint a batch of tokens with length `batch_size` for `to`.
337	    /// Returns the token id of the first token minted in the batch; if
338	    /// `batch_size` is 0, returns the number of consecutive ids minted so
339	    /// far.
340	    ///
341	    /// CAUTION: Does not emit a [`Transfer`] event. This is ERC-721 compliant
342	    /// as long as it is done inside of the constructor, which is enforced by
343	    /// this function.
344	    ///
345	    /// CAUTION: Does not invoke
346	    /// [`erc721::IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] on the receiver.
347	    ///
348	    /// # Arguments
349	    ///
350	    /// * `&self` - Write access to the contract's state.
351	    /// * `token_id` - Token id as a number.
352	    ///
353	    /// # Errors
354	    ///
355	    /// * [`erc721::Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If `to` is [`Address::ZERO`].
356	    /// * [`Error::ExceededMaxBatchMint`] - If `batch_size` exceeds
357	    ///   `max_batch_size` of the contract.
358	    ///
359	    /// # Events
360	    ///
361	    /// * [`ConsecutiveTransfer`].
362	    pub fn _mint_consecutive(
363	        &mut self,
364	        to: Address,
365	        batch_size: U96,
366	    ) -> Result<U96, Error> {
367	        let next = self._next_consecutive_id();
368	
369	        // Minting a batch of size 0 is a no-op.
370	        if batch_size > U96::ZERO {
371	            if to.is_zero() {
372	                return Err(erc721::Error::InvalidReceiver(
373	                    ERC721InvalidReceiver { receiver: Address::ZERO },
374	                )
375	                .into());
376	            }
377	
378	            if batch_size > self._max_batch_size() {
379	                return Err(ERC721ExceededMaxBatchMint {
380	                    batch_size: U256::from(batch_size),
381	                    max_batch: U256::from(self._max_batch_size())}
382	                .into());
383	            }
384	
385	            // Push an ownership checkpoint & emit event.
386	            let last = next + batch_size - uint!(1_U96);
387	            self.sequential_ownership.push(last, to.into())?;
388	
389	            // The invariant required by this function is preserved because the
390	            // new sequential_ownership checkpoint is attributing
391	            // ownership of `batch_size` new tokens to account `to`.
392	            self.erc721._increase_balance(
393	                to,
394	                alloy_primitives::U128::from(batch_size),
395	            );
396	
397	            self.vm().log(ConsecutiveTransfer {
398	                from_token_id: next.to::<U256>(),
399	                to_token_id: last.to::<U256>(),
400	                from_address: Address::ZERO,
401	                to_address: to});
402	        }
403	        Ok(next)
404	    }

406	    /// Override of [`Erc721::_update`] that restricts normal minting to after
407	    /// construction.
408	    ///
409	    /// # Arguments
410	    ///
411	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
412	    /// * `to` - Account of the recipient.
413	    /// * `token_id` - Token id as a number.
414	    /// * `auth` - Account used for authorization of the update.
415	    ///
416	    /// # Errors
417	    ///
418	    /// * [`erc721::Error::NonexistentToken`] - If token does not exist and
419	    ///   `auth` is not [`Address::ZERO`].
420	    /// * [`erc721::Error::InsufficientApproval`] - If `auth` is not
421	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`] and `auth` does not have a right to approve this
422	    ///   token.
423	    ///
424	    /// # Events
425	    ///
426	    /// * [`Transfer`].
427	    pub fn _update(
428	        &mut self,
429	        to: Address,
430	        token_id: U256,
431	        auth: Address,
432	    ) -> Result<Address, Error> {
433	        let previous_owner = self._update_base(to, token_id, auth)?;
434	
435	        // if we burn
436	        if to.is_zero()
437	            // and the token_id was minted in a batch
438	            && token_id < U256::from(self._next_consecutive_id())
439	            // and the token was never marked as burnt
440	            && !self.sequential_burn.get(token_id)
441	        {
442	            // record burn
443	            self.sequential_burn.set(token_id);
444	        }
445	
446	        Ok(previous_owner)
447	    }

585	    /// * [`erc721::Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If `to` is [`Address::ZERO`], or
586	    ///   [`erc721::IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] hasn't returned its
587	    ///   interface id or returned with error.
588	    ///
589	    /// # Events
590	    ///
591	    /// * [`Transfer`].
592	    pub fn _safe_mint(
593	        &mut self,
594	        to: Address,
595	        token_id: U256,
596	        data: &Bytes,
597	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
598	        self._mint(to, token_id)?;
599	        Ok(self.erc721._check_on_erc721_received(
600	            self.vm().msg_sender(),
601	            Address::ZERO,
602	            to,
603	            token_id,
604	            data,
605	        )?)
606	    }

608	    /// Destroys `token_id`.
609	    ///
610	    /// The approval is cleared when the token is burned. This is an
611	    /// internal function that does not check if the sender is authorized
612	    /// to operate on the token.
613	    ///
614	    /// # Arguments
615	    ///
616	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
617	    /// * `token_id` - Token id as a number.
618	    ///
619	    /// # Errors
620	    ///
621	    /// * [`erc721::Error::NonexistentToken`] - If token does not exist.
622	    ///
623	    /// # Events
624	    ///
625	    /// * [`Transfer`].
626	    pub fn _burn(&mut self, token_id: U256) -> Result<(), Error> {
627	        let previous_owner =
628	            self._update(Address::ZERO, token_id, Address::ZERO)?;
629	        if previous_owner.is_zero() {
630	            return Err(erc721::Error::NonexistentToken(
631	                ERC721NonexistentToken { token_id },
632	            )
633	            .into());
634	        }
635	        Ok(())
636	    }
